first_prompt:
Create a high-resolution FOUR-PANEL 2x2 art-direction concept sheet for the Critical Shift medical/reanimation room. The references are a rigorous design constraint. FIVE REFERENCE CONTACT SHEETS contain 22 original renders. Sheet 1: existing medical room, four corner cutaways. Sheet 2: medical room, all four walls. Sheet 3: five primary medical assets, OCRU, restart, cartridges, reserve, decon. Sheet 4: five support assets, recovery, rescue cart, supplies, wash, cabinet. Sheet 5: four approved overhauled SPAWN ROOM views, hall, warm briefing, lockers and close material/dressing detail. All 18 medical views and all four spawn views must inform the result. Inspect and use ALL supplied references. Medical images define the UNCHANGED layout and boundaries; spawn images define the material fidelity, color families, construction detail and lived-in prop richness to match.

ROOM FUNCTION: This is where incapacitated or biologically offline/dead cooperative-game workers are revived in the Organic Continuity and Recommissioning Unit (OCRU). The large OCRU loading bed on the WEST/LEFT side is the functional hero. The simple cot on the right is a secondary recovery berth. No medical instructions or diagrams; this is fictional game environment art.

IMMUTABLE LAYOUT: Keep the existing 8m wide x 9m deep x 3.6m high room and rear-right decontamination alcove, walls, floor footprint and centered front entry. Preserve equipment positions and clear central rescue/cart route. OCRU along the west wall; restart console against the rear wall slightly left of center; cartridge bank to its right; reserve-power cabinet to console's left; decon alcove rear-right; recovery cot east/right middle; handwash between recovery and the front-right supplies workbench; supplies cabinet east/right rear; transfer cart front-left. Do not enlarge the room, add doors/windows, move the bed to the center, replace the room with a spaceship, or merge it with the spawn room. Revamp all materials, modeling richness and local art while keeping these placements recognizable.

VISUAL TARGET: AAA-level ENVIRONMENT-ART CRAFT and asset detail, while deliberately STYLIZED, in a VALORANT-INSPIRED grounded semi-realistic environmental art language. Crisp planar surfaces, sharp authoritative silhouettes, strong structural masses, folded sheet metal, reinforced frames, deliberate angular profiles, recessed panel layers, distinct secondary forms and carefully placed tertiary detail. Believable adult-human scale. Specific manufacturing logic on every asset. Broad stylized roughness and paint variation, shaped fabric folds, worn corners, screws, hinges, catches, seals, labels, analog gauges, cable glands, hose coupling, service hatch layers, medical cartridge construction, hand tools, gauze packets, bandage rolls, cartridge wrappers, restrained paperwork, a battered cup, spare parts, and sparse maintenance evidence. These must look handcrafted, not repeated cubes. Subtle construction-appropriate edge finishing is allowed; avoid pillowy rounded boxes, universal bevels, inflated plastic toys, low-poly web/Three.js demo appearance, generic sci-fi kitbash, holograms and neon greebles. Do NOT copy Valorant's proprietary assets or a particular map. This is premium original stylized game art, not photographic horror film realism.

MATCH SPAWN COLORS AND DETAIL: Retain the project's muted mauve plaster, deep navy lower-wall protection, muted institutional blue, terracotta/oxide painted equipment, warm off-white cloth and paperwork, gray bare metal, charcoal rubber, and small ochre/hazard-yellow accents. The spawn room's cozy cheer is manipulative corporate preparation for a supposedly fun shift; this medical room reveals the bleak, hopeless reality. Use those same color/material families in darkness, with fading, water marks, repaired paint and restrained corrosion; do not wash the whole room into generic gray. It was once a properly established, well-built industrial medical facility, now degraded by neglect and disturbing events.

LIGHTING: The overall room is DARK. Exactly ONE red practical light above the OCRU reanimation/loading bed creates the strongest focal pool, catching the bed surface, rails, couplings and gantry with crimson light; shadows and color must sell the single source. The recovery cot is not the red-lit focal bed. Add ONE dim warm amber task light on the right/front supply workbench or its cabinet, grazing tools and supplies. Add ONE OR TWO dim controlled directional/spot accents to reveal the restart console and decon entrance without flattening the room. Other inherited ceiling fixtures are mostly dead/off, visibly worn. Maintain deep shadow, strong hierarchy, readable navigation and soft bounced fill; don't make every corner equally lit or every surface glow. No extra dominant red lamps. Art-directed material separation remains clear despite darkness.

NEGLECT AND HORROR: Mix restrained implication with a few overt clues. Selective dried maroon blood traces on the loading rail/floor or a glove, old cleaning marks, chipped wall protection, small leaks, repair patches, abandoned supplies and dated service tags. No random rubble carpet, no blood-soaked walls, no exposed organs or graphic human remains. Hide a closed dark charcoal fabric BODY BAG under the OCRU bed, behind the lower chassis/lifting supports: at least 85% occluded, only a sliver and one folded handle visible from ordinary views. Attach one tiny faded ochre sticky note near that concealed edge, partly blocked by a rail and in shadow; it is an easter egg players have to search for, not an obvious story prop or large caption. Tiny note reads 'EARLY CLOCK-OUT DENIED' if close enough to decipher. Do not put the bag on top of the bed or conspicuously in the center aisle. Keep the treatment bed empty and its functional rescue access clear.

FOUR PANELS, CONSISTENT ROOM:
A, top-left: wide player-eye-height entry view, OCRU on left under the single red light; recovery and warm supply area on right; restart/decon rear; correct reference layout.
B, top-right: reverse wide room view from the rear toward the existing centered entry, consistent assets and lighting; show decline and preserved central lane.
C, bottom-left: substantial OCRU hero close-up showing redesigned angular gantry, bed, rail, mechanisms, realistic material variety and precision small details under the single red pool. The concealed body bag/sticky note may be barely discoverable at the shadowed lower edge; don't spotlight them.
D, bottom-right: warm workbench/support-area hero with cabinet, wash edge and recovery context, rich practical medical supplies and a few purposeful human/maintenance props; the red bed may appear softly in distant background, not a second red source.

Use clean thin dividers and unobtrusive small panel labels only: 'ENTRY', 'REVERSE', 'OCRU', 'SUPPORT'. Fill each panel with the image, not essays, swatches or giant titles. Show premium high-fidelity stylized environment concept quality, controlled visual density, authoritative industrial shapes, atmospheric depth, tactile surfaces and coherent lighting. This is a concept proposal for the existing room, never a new layout.

HORROR BALANCE: Reduce the conspicuous blood spread on the floor by about 85%.
